findings.title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
findings.summary_md: Google Cloud's GTIG and Mandiant, working with ManageEngine's METAL lab, disclosed that threat cluster UNC7017 conducted repeated short-burst (five to ten minute) configuration tampering on AOMEI origin servers between April and July 2026. During each window the attacker modified down_html.ini and Notifycfg.ini to redirect AOMEI Backupper clients to a malicious upgrade-now.zip carrying the CROSSROAD downloader and SHINYROAD backdoor, then reverted the files to authentic content. The report documents three confirmed windows (May 28, July 16, July 20) plus a WebDAV NTLM credential coercion vector and extensive indicators of compromise. Published October 16, 2026.

findings.title: AOMEI Backupper supply-chain compromise: Investigation and analysis
findings.summary_md: ManageEngine's METAL lab published its analysis of the UNC7017 campaign against AOMEI update infrastructure, describing how attackers changed both the download URL and the expected version number and MD5 checksum in the remote configuration file so clients would accept a malicious ZIP archive. Researchers confirmed three brief tampering windows of ten, six, and five minutes but note more may have occurred, and the same infrastructure also serves AnyViewer customers. METAL first detected the activity in late May and notified AOMEI in early June. Published October 16, 2026.

findings.title: Attackers Tampered with AOMEI Backupper's Update Servers for Minutes to Deliver a Backdoor
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported that attackers repeatedly changed the files AOMEI Backupper fetches from vendor update servers in five to ten minute windows between May and July 2026, so any copy that checked for an update during one of those windows would download and run a backdoor. The coverage notes neither configuration file is cryptographically verified by the client and the checksum meant to validate the archive sits in the same unauthenticated file that names it. Published October 16, 2026.

findings.title: Hackers hijack AOMEI update servers to secretly spread malware
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported that UNC7017 briefly tampered with AOMEI's down_html.ini and Notifycfg.ini between April and July 2026 to redirect AOMEI Backupper clients to a malicious ZIP archive distributing CROSSROAD and SHINYROAD. The attacks were first detected on May 28 when ManageEngine spotted AOMEI Backupper suddenly installing the legitimate Radmin remote administration tool on computers at two unrelated companies in different countries. Published October 19, 2026.
